acceptance: A PR whose head predates the probe's posting contract, with a base that contains it, gets a correct 'release-v2 probe' status or a clear failure naming the fix, shown by a workflow test or a live PR from an old base.
A stacked PR whose base also predates the contract keeps working (base and head scripts agree).
docs describing release-v2-probe.yml state which revision's launch script runs and why the verdict script needs no change.
context:
2026-11-20 evidence: #4382 (branch from before #4390) failed run 44648125958 twice with the same 403 (`gh api --method POST failed: Resource not accessible by integration`), attempt 2 included, after `make pr-arm` closed and reopened the PR to start CI on a fresh merge ref. github-actions then disabled auto-merge (00:50:39Z). The checkout step takes `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, so the merge ref's workflow (statuses: write) ran the head's older check-run script. Workaround used: merge origin/develop into the branch. At least nine failing runs from 2026-11-19T20:48Z to 2026-11-20T00:43Z were the same 403.

2026-11-20 live check: the probe passes on every PR whose head contains #4390 (9da6e1c448), for example #4322 and #4393, and fails with HTTP 403 on heads that do not: #4340 (fc8766c7) and #4331 (41bc621c). Updating a branch from develop clears it.

2026-11-20 owner-approved correction: evidence rule restated (base contains 9da6e1c4, head lacks it; stacked #4384/#4385 explained), the overstated claim that a base checkout stops a PR controlling its own status removed (pull_request uses the merge ref's workflow, which the PR can edit), and the proposal narrowed to the launch step. Live state 2026-11-20: #4322 now contains 9da6e1c4 and passes; #4331 lacks it but has a passing 'release-v2 probe' check run from the old launcher (whether the ruleset, which requires the context from integration 15368, counts it is unverified); #4340 lacks it and has no probe result; #4384 and #4385 are drafts stacked on #4322, #4385 conflicting.
description:
#4390 (merge 9da6e1c4, 2026-11-19T20:48Z) switched the required 'release-v2 probe' from a check run to a commit status and changed the dispatch job's permissions from checks: write to statuses: write. For pull_request events the workflow definition, and so the token permissions, comes from the merge ref, but release-v2-probe.yml checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha and runs that tree's scripts/release_probe_launch.py. When the PR's base contains 9da6e1c4 and its head does not, the head's old launcher POSTs repos/.../check-runs with a statuses-only token and gets 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' (inferred from the head's code and the job's token permissions; the log does not name the URL), so the required status is never posted and an armed PR cannot merge. Observed on #4393 (feat/polars-matrix-2-1; fixed by merging develop, after which the status posted 'No release input changed'), #4322, #4331 and #4340, all with heads lacking 9da6e1c4 and base develop. #4384 and #4385 also lack it but passed, because they are stacked on #4322, whose branch also lacked it, so their merge ref carried the old workflow (their token logs show Checks: write) and the old script together. The rule is therefore: the probe fails when the PR's base contains 9da6e1c4 and its head does not. Immediate remedy for an affected PR: merge or rebase its base and push. Not a token-settings or repository-rename problem.

Decision gate: run the launch script from the base revision (a second checkout of github.event.pull_request.base.sha) while the job graph check keeps reading the head's release-v2.yml; or keep the head script and fail with a clear 'merge your base branch' message when the head's launcher predates the workflow contract. Only the launch step needs this: the verdict script runs in release-v2.yml's report job, dispatched on the branch, where workflow and script both come from the head and cannot disagree. Running the launcher from base does not stop a PR from controlling its own required status, because on pull_request the workflow file itself comes from the merge ref and a PR can edit it; the change removes the version skew only.

Guardrails: the required context stays a commit status; do not grant checks: write back as a workaround; fork refusal unchanged; the graph check must still validate the head's release-v2.yml.
